title: Machine Enable & Permissives (Safety Architecture)
concept:
A machine should only run when every safety and process condition is healthy.
You gate a machine-enable seal-in with those conditions ANDed in -- and, like
a stop, healthy safety signals are wired NORMALLY-CLOSED, so you AND them as-is
(never invert):

    Machine_Enable := (Start_PB OR Machine_Enable)
                      AND Safety_OK AND Guard_Closed AND Air_OK;

Any condition going FALSE drops the machine out immediately. Because it's a
seal-in, restoring the condition does NOT auto-restart -- the operator must
press Start again. That deliberate restart is a safety feature.

IMPORTANT SAFETY NOTE: a standard PLC must NOT be the sole E-stop. The E-stop
function belongs to a safety relay or safety PLC (Allen-Bradley GuardLogix,
Siemens F-CPU) wired to rated safety devices per ISO 13850 / ISO 13849-1. Here
Safety_OK is a MONITORED status coming FROM that safety system into your normal
logic -- you're gating the machine enable, not implementing the E-stop.

Each permissive is read with XIC (as-is). Using XIO (NOT) on a healthy-when-TRUE safety signal would defeat the fail-safe wiring, so never invert them.
ab_note:
In Studio 5000, Safety_OK typically comes from a GuardLogix safety task or a
safety relay's monitored output. Your standard-task ST reads it as a BOOL and
ANDs it (with process permissives) into the enable. Guard interlocks and
E-stops should be electrically separate, not daisy-chained on one input.
siemens_note:
In TIA Portal, the safety function lives in an F-CPU / safety program (F-DBs,
F-blocks). The standard program reads the passivated/monitored safe status and
gates the enable with permissives -- same :=, AND, OR.
task:
Given Start_PB (N.O.), and the healthy-when-TRUE signals Safety_OK, Guard_Closed
and Air_OK, plus output Machine_Enable, write ONE seal-in assignment so:

    - Machine_Enable latches on when Start_PB is pressed AND all conditions OK
    - It holds after Start releases
    - Any of Safety_OK / Guard_Closed / Air_OK going FALSE drops it out
    - After a condition is restored it stays OFF until Start is pressed again

All three conditions are healthy-when-TRUE -- AND them in as-is, no NOT.
starter:
(* Lesson 06 -- Machine Enable & Permissives (Safety Architecture) *)
(* Wiring key:  N.O. contact -> read AS-IS (XIC)   |   N.C. contact -> AS-IS, fail-safe (XIC)   |   NOT x = XIO *)

VAR
    Start_PB       : BOOL;  (* N.O. start PB      -> XIC (as-is)                     *)
    Safety_OK      : BOOL;  (* from safety relay  -> XIC (as-is): TRUE = safe        *)
    Guard_Closed   : BOOL;  (* N.C. guard switch  -> XIC (as-is): TRUE = closed      *)
    Air_OK         : BOOL;  (* pressure switch    -> XIC (as-is): TRUE = pressure OK *)
    Machine_Enable : BOOL;  (* output                                               *)
END_VAR

(* ----- YOUR LOGIC : write your answer between these two lines ----- *)
    (* TODO: one seal-in enable rung; AND the healthy-when-TRUE permissives in AS-IS (XIC), never inverted. *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------ *)

checks.hint: Safety_OK is TRUE when healthy -- no NOT.
Guard_Closed is TRUE when shut -- no NOT.
Air_OK is TRUE when adequate -- no NOT.

checks.message: Executed: enables only with all conditions OK; any drop stops it; no auto-restart
checks.hint: Latch on Start with all OK; drop on any condition FALSE; require a fresh Start to re-enable.

solution:
(* Lesson 06 -- Machine Enable & Permissives (Safety Architecture) *)
(* Wiring key:  N.O. contact -> read AS-IS (XIC)   |   N.C. contact -> AS-IS, fail-safe (XIC)   |   NOT x = XIO *)

VAR
    Start_PB       : BOOL;  (* N.O. start PB      -> XIC (as-is)                     *)
    Safety_OK      : BOOL;  (* from safety relay  -> XIC (as-is): TRUE = safe        *)
    Guard_Closed   : BOOL;  (* N.C. guard switch  -> XIC (as-is): TRUE = closed      *)
    Air_OK         : BOOL;  (* pressure switch    -> XIC (as-is): TRUE = pressure OK *)
    Machine_Enable : BOOL;  (* output                                               *)
END_VAR

(* ----- YOUR LOGIC : write your answer between these two lines ----- *)
Machine_Enable := (Start_PB OR Machine_Enable) AND Safety_OK AND Guard_Closed AND Air_OK;
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------ *)
